headline: High: open-webui’s broad egress, browser/subprocess/tooling, and shared-session state create dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflict, and unverified actioning with haystack.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, and open-webui exposes MCP, plugins, tools, and OpenAPI servers. That creates a plausible instruction-bridging path where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF haystack ingests open-webui output through MCP or REST without provenance tagging
IF open-webui forwards haystack-generated content into tool prompts or plugin inputs
mitigations: Disable MCP/tool ingestion between the two agents
Add a strict allowlist for tool-call schemas
Prefix all cross-agent content as untrusted data
Review one sample end-to-end prompt path before deployment

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and open-webui handles files, documents, notes, persistent memory, and API keys while also calling many external services. If they share a workspace or session path, open-webui can expose sensitive material and haystack can transmit it outward. The default blast radius includes secrets and documents, so this is high.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same mounted files or workspace
IF open-webui loads documents or API keys that haystack can access through shared storage
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mount points immediately
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Run haystack with egress allowlists only
Disable file ingestion on the shared path
Rotate any API keys exposed to open-webui

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress, while open-webui can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and has persistent shared web-app sessions with Redis-backed multi-worker state. Those overlapping mutable surfaces can race on shared resources or session state, and the profile does not show locking. Uncertainty about orchestration means we should choose the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same files, session store, or MCP-backed resource
IF open-webui is deployed with multiple workers sharing Redis state while haystack concurrently mutates shared outputs
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Use per-agent session namespaces
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Add a lock around any shared MCP resource
Test one concurrent write collision in staging

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can generate retrieved facts, and open-webui is a web UI that can render or act on model outputs through tools and function calling. If open-webui treats haystack output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or user-visible decisions. The interaction is plausible by default, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF open-webui passes haystack output into tools, plugins, or function calls without verification
IF haystack-generated claims are displayed or executed as authoritative in open-webui
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions
Require citations for any retrieved claim
Mark haystack output as untrusted in the UI
Disable auto-execution of tool calls
Log and diff source passages against rendered claims

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics, while open-webui touches prompts, chat messages, documents, notes, calendar events, files, API keys, and persistent memory. The pair therefore concentrates multiple data classes in one workflow, and open-webui’s broad external integrations raise retention and residency mismatch risk. No direct residency violation is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated or customer data is routed through open-webui’s external connectors
IF retention or deletion expectations differ between haystack logs and open-webui memory/files
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Disable persistent memory for regulated data
Align retention settings across both systems
Restrict external connectors to approved regions
Document deletion/export handling for shared data
